key: A chai-stall owner near a Bengaluru
name: ch03_coffee_board_tech_park
alt: Office workers hurrying past a tech-park coffee stall stop to read a board that promises filter coffee in two minutes before their 10 a.m. stand-up.
scene: A wide street-level view of a pavement outside a glass-fronted tech park in Bengaluru, bright early morning, a tall office tower with blue windows in the background and a few rain trees along the road. On the LEFT, a small wooden coffee stall with a striped awning, a steel coffee boiler with a tap, a row of steel tumblers and davaras on the counter. Behind it the owner, a smiling man in his forties in a cream half-sleeve shirt and a checked lungi, pours coffee from a height with a long arc of brown liquid. He is calm and quiet, not shouting. In the CENTRE, standing on the pavement facing the walkers, a chalk sandwich board reads "COFFEE IN 2 MIN" with a small drawing of a steaming tumbler and a wall clock showing a few minutes before ten. On the RIGHT, three office workers with lanyards and laptop bags (a young woman in a kurta checking her phone, a man in a blue shirt mid-stride, an older man with spectacles) have turned their heads towards the board; one is already reaching for his wallet. A thought bubble above them shows a small clock at ten and a meeting table. Dashed arrows run from the board's words to their bubble, showing the message is about their morning. Warm golden light, brisk but friendly mood. Label: "THEIR MORNING" in bold above the workers on the right.

key: Getting a toddler into the car seat
name: ch03_toddler_car_seat_cows
alt: Split picture: parents push a screaming rigid toddler into a car seat, then the grandmother offers her the job of spotting cows and she climbs in happily.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the open rear door of a white family hatchback parked outside an apartment building at dawn, suitcases and a tiffin bag on the roof rack, ready for a family drive to a temple town. LEFT panel: a toddler girl (about two, yellow frock, tiny pigtails) is stiff as a plank, arched backwards, mouth wide open screaming, with small tear drops; the father (thirties, grey T-shirt) pushes her shoulders down into a blue child seat while the mother (green salwar kameez) tugs at the straps, both frowning and sweating. A red cross badge floats above. Label "PUSH" at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: the same car, the same toddler now climbing into the seat by herself, beaming, holding a small fold-down window shade like a flag; the grandmother (sixties, white-and-maroon cotton sari, spectacles, grey bun) leans in at the door, smiling, pointing out of the window. An inset bubble shows a cow standing by a country road, which is what the child is now in charge of spotting. The parents stand behind, relieved, arms down. A green tick floats above. Label "OFFER" at the top of the right panel. Soft early-morning light, warm family mood.

key: Your aunt donates generously to the temple
name: ch03_aunt_temple_donor_board
alt: An aunt offers money at a temple renovation counter while three thought bubbles show her devotion, her family name on the donor board, and the watching neighbours.
scene: A medium-wide view inside a South Indian temple courtyard under renovation, bamboo scaffolding along a half-painted gopuram in the background, a brass oil lamp and a row of marigold garlands. In the CENTRE, an aunt in her fifties (rich maroon silk sari, gold bangles, jasmine in her hair, a small handbag) stands at a wooden donation table, handing over an envelope with both hands to a priest in a white dhoti with a sacred thread and sandal paste on his forehead, who writes in a receipt book. Above the aunt rise THREE small thought bubbles in a fan, each with one clear picture: the first shows folded hands in front of a small lamp, the second shows a wooden donor board with gold-painted rows of names and her family's row glowing, the third shows two neighbour ladies whispering and watching. On the RIGHT wall the real donor board hangs, a dark wood panel with gold lines, one line freshly highlighted. On the LEFT, two neighbour women in cotton saris stand near a pillar holding puja plates, glancing over. Thin dashed lines link each bubble to its real-world counterpart in the scene. Warm afternoon light, gentle and sincere mood, not mocking: all three wants are real. Label: "THREE WANTS" in bold at the top centre above the bubbles.

key: A family WhatsApp group where the cousins
name: ch03_family_group_goa_trip
alt: Split picture: a family chat where a call-home request gets no replies, then an uncle's trip offer gets a flood of replies from cousins in hostels.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. Each half shows a large smartphone screen of a generic family group chat (no app logo), with a green-tinted header and speech bubbles. LEFT panel: on the screen, one lonely grey message bubble from a mother with a small saree-clad avatar reads only "call home?"; below it the chat is empty with two grey ticks. Around the phone, three small figures of college students in hostel rooms (a boy on a bunk bed with headphones, a girl at a desk with books, a boy playing on a laptop) ignore their phones, which lie face down. A tiny cobweb hangs from the corner of the phone. Label "0 REPLIES" at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: the same phone, now an uncle's bubble with a small plane icon and a beach umbrella drawing reads "Goa trip?", and below it a tall stack of coloured reply bubbles spills out of the top of the screen with thumbs-up and raised-hand icons. The same three students now sit up straight, phones in hand, typing eagerly with big smiles, little exclamation marks above their heads. A dashed arrow runs from the trip bubble to each student. Bright cheerful light. Label "12 REPLIES" at the top of the right panel.

key: A child who refuses to start swimming lessons
name: ch03_swim_pool_cousins_fun
alt: A child stands at the edge of a society pool watching cousins splash and race, and starts wanting to join instead of being lectured.
scene: A wide view of a blue rectangular swimming pool in an Indian apartment society on a sunny Sunday morning, tiled edges, a lifeguard chair, a couple of potted palms and tower blocks in the background. In the POOL on the right half, three cousins (a girl about ten in a purple swimsuit and goggles, a boy about twelve with a swim cap, a younger boy with orange armbands) splash, race and laugh with big open mouths, water droplets flying, one doing a cannonball from the edge. On the LEFT at the pool's edge, a boy about seven sits on the tiles in shorts and a T-shirt, knees hugged, toes just touching the water, leaning forward with wide curious eyes. A thought bubble above him shows himself floating on his back, smiling. Behind him his mother (thirties, cotton kurta, sunglasses on her head) stands calmly holding a towel and a small swimming-class timetable card, not lecturing, just letting him watch. A large curved dashed arrow runs from the laughing cousins to the watching boy, showing the fun pulling him in. A small poolside board reads "CLASS MON 6 PM". Bright sparkling sunlight, joyful mood. Label: "MAKE IT FUN" in bold at the top centre above the pool.

key: Your landlord in Pune announces a
name: ch03_landlord_cost_list
alt: A tenant sits with his landlord over tea and shows him a written list of the landlord's own costs of losing a reliable tenant.
scene: A medium view of a modest Pune apartment living room, a ceiling fan, a window with a balcony grille and potted tulsi, a sofa and a low wooden table with two cups of tea and a plate of biscuits. On the LEFT, the landlord, a man in his sixties in a white kurta and spectacles, sits in an armchair with arms crossed, a renewal agreement on his knee showing a big red upward arrow. On the RIGHT, the tenant, a calm man in his early thirties in a blue checked shirt, leans forward and holds out a sheet of paper towards the landlord, turned so the landlord can read it. The sheet is enlarged in an inset bubble in the CENTRE TOP: a simple list with four lines and tiny icons: an empty flat with a calendar ("2 MONTHS EMPTY"), a broker with a rupee coin ("BROKER FEE"), a paint roller ("REPAINT"), and a question-mark stranger ("STRANGER"). Beside the list a smaller column shows a calendar with three years of green ticks for rent paid on time, captioned "3 YEARS" and "ON TIME". The landlord's expression is turning from stern to thoughtful, one eyebrow raised, hand moving to his chin. A dashed arrow runs from the list to the landlord's head. Warm evening lamp light, calm negotiating mood. Label: "HIS SIDE" in bold above the inset list.

name: ch03_society_notice_ps
alt: Residents in front of a long self-centred society notice all look straight past it to the one line at the bottom that offers them a covered parking spot.
scene: A medium view of a housing-society lobby in Gurugram, a glass entrance door, a mailbox wall and a large green-felt notice board on a pillar. On the notice board, one long white sheet is pinned with a heavy header bar and many dense grey lines of text, with the word "COMMITTEE" repeated in bold on several lines, an official round stamp and a signature. At the very bottom, a short line in a bright yellow highlight reads "P.S." next to a small icon of a car under a roof. In FRONT of the board stand four residents seen from behind and three-quarters: a woman in a gym outfit holding a yoga mat, an older man in a cardigan with a walking stick, a young man with car keys, and a mother holding a toddler. Dotted sight lines run from each of their eyes directly to the yellow P.S. line, skipping the grey text. Two of them have small irritated scribble clouds above their heads aimed at the top of the notice; the young man smiles at the car icon. On the floor a security guard's stool and a parking-sticker box. Cool fluorescent lobby light, wry mood. Labels: "WE, WE, WE" beside the top of the notice, and "THEIR WANT" with an arrow pointing at the P.S. line.

key: A school sends parents a note
name: ch03_school_drop_note
alt: Split picture: a parent frowns at a school note about the school's traffic problem, then smiles at a note about her child getting a calm start before the gate jams.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, each half showing a mother (late thirties, office kurta, handbag, car keys) at a breakfast table at home reading a printed school note, her son (about eight, school uniform with a tie and backpack) eating idli beside her. LEFT panel: the note she holds is filled with dense lines and a small drawing of a jammed school gate with the school's building and a red administration stamp; she frowns, sighs and sets it aside, sipping tea and looking at the clock. A grey cloud of jammed cars floats above the note, centred on the school, not on her. Label "OUR PROBLEM" at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: the same mother reading a different note that shows a small drawing of her child standing happily in a morning assembly line and a clock reading "7:50"; a little inset shows a car exiting a clear lane with a green tick. She smiles, checks her watch and is already standing, picking up the car keys, the boy grabbing his backpack. A dashed arrow runs from the note's picture of the child to the boy beside her. Early morning kitchen light, calm and practical mood. Label "YOUR CHILD" at the top of the right panel.

key: Two candidates email the same Bengaluru
name: ch03_two_job_emails
alt: Split picture: a startup CTO ignores an email about what the candidate wants and forwards an email about the company's festival-sale traffic problem.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same startup CTO (mid-thirties, black T-shirt, short beard, rimless spectacles) at a standing desk with a large monitor in an open-plan Bengaluru office with beanbags and a whiteboard behind. LEFT panel: the monitor shows an email whose lines are all decorated with small icons of the sender: a stick figure climbing stairs, a book, a rupee bag. Above the email float three small bubbles, each showing the word "I". The CTO leans back, bored, finger on the delete key, with a small trash can icon receiving the email. Label "ABOUT ME" at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: the monitor shows a second email with a small chart of a traffic spike shaped like a mountain, a shopping cart icon and a shield holding the spike steady. The CTO leans in, eyebrows up, and clicks a forward arrow; a dashed arrow carries the email to a hiring manager (a woman in her thirties in a teal top) at the next desk, who looks up with interest. A green tick badge floats over the shield. Bright office daylight, sharp and clear mood. Label "ABOUT YOU" at the top of the right panel.

key: Two sabziwalas at the same Sunday market
name: ch03_sabziwala_mango_pitch
alt: Split picture: one vegetable seller calls out prices to nobody, while another holds up the season's first mango to a regular customer, who fills her bag.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves in the same busy Sunday street market under blue tarpaulin awnings, wooden carts heaped with produce, strings of bulbs overhead. LEFT panel: a vegetable seller (forties, vest and lungi, towel on shoulder) sits slumped behind a big pile of onions and tomatoes on a cart, hand cupped at his mouth calling out, with small price-tag cards stuck into the piles. Shoppers walk past without turning their heads; a dashed line shows his voice falling flat on the ground. Label "PRICES" at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: a second seller (fifties, white kurta, cheerful moustache) stands at his cart stacked with golden mangoes in straw-lined crates, leaning forward and holding one ripe mango up towards a regular customer, an elderly aunty in a printed cotton sari with a cloth shopping bag. A thought bubble above her shows two small grandchildren eating mangoes. She is tasting a slice he cut for her, smiling, and her bag is bulging with mangoes. A small sign on his cart reads "FIRST OF SEASON". A green tick floats above. Warm morning sunlight, lively and friendly mood. Label "HER WANT" at the top of the right panel.

name: ch03_compost_terrace_visit
alt: A society secretary shows three families a neighbouring society's terrace garden full of tomatoes and coriander grown on its own compost.
scene: A wide view of a sunny apartment rooftop terrace in an Indian city, water tanks and a dish antenna at the back, a low parapet and the tops of neighbouring towers in the distance. Across the terrace stand raised beds overflowing with red tomatoes on stakes, leafy coriander, chillies and brinjals, and at the RIGHT end three green compost bins with a small hand-painted sign "COMPOST". A resident gardener from that society (sixties, straw hat, rolled-up sleeves) hands out a small basket of tomatoes. In the CENTRE, the visiting secretary (fifties, half-sleeve shirt, spectacles, clipboard tucked under his arm, not reading from it) gestures proudly towards the beds. On the LEFT, three visiting family members (a young mother holding a basket, a father with a toddler on his shoulders, a teenage girl taking a photo on her phone) look amazed, mouths open, one already tasting a cherry tomato. A dashed arrow loops from the compost bins through the soil to the tomatoes and on to the basket, showing kitchen scraps becoming food. A small inset in the top-left corner shows their own society's ignored notice on a board with a cobweb. Bright late-morning sun, hopeful mood. Label: "SEE IT" in bold at the top centre.

key: A colleague posts in the office group
name: ch03_sunday_cricket_posts
alt: Split picture: a complaint-filled cricket invite draws four people, while an invite about chai, vada pav and full teams fills the turf with fourteen players.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. Each half has a large phone screen near the top showing a generic office group chat bubble (no app logo), and a small box-cricket turf with green netting below it. LEFT panel: the bubble shows a sad face, a bandaged finger icon and the number "4"; below, on an almost empty turf, three lonely players stand slumped, one of them with a bandaged finger and a bat dragging, the stumps leaning, under a grey sky. Label "MY PROBLEM" at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: the bubble shows a sunrise with "7 AM", a small steaming chai glass, a vada pav, and a row of tiny player icons; below, the turf is full: five or six players in colourful T-shirts in mid-game, a batsman swinging, a bowler running in, two people waiting by a bench with chai glasses and a paper plate of vada pav, everyone smiling, morning sunlight. A sign-up counter beside the phone shows "14" with a green tick. A dashed arrow runs from the bubble to the turf. Bright morning light on the right, flat greyish light on the left. Label "YOUR SUNDAY" at the top of the right panel.

name: ch03_milk_bowler_bones
alt: A father shows his cricket-loving daughter that fast bowlers need strong bones, and she gulps down the glass of milk she refused.
scene: A medium view of a breakfast table in a Chennai home in the morning, a window with a kolam on the doorstep outside, a wall calendar and a small cricket bat leaning against the wall. On the LEFT, the father (late thirties, white vest and veshti, spectacles pushed up) holds a steel tumbler of filter coffee in one hand and with the other points at a picture on his phone: a generic fast bowler in mid-delivery, no team logo. An inset bubble above the phone shows a simple bone shape with a small lightning bolt beside a cricket ball, meaning strong bones make fast bowling. On the RIGHT, his daughter (seven, two plaits with ribbons, school uniform pinafore, a cricket cap on her head) tips back a big glass of milk, eyes closed in determination, a milk moustache forming, one hand already curled into a bowling grip on the table. Next to her glass sits a small red rubber ball. In the background, the mother, in a cotton sari, peeks from the kitchen doorway smiling. A small faded bubble near the girl shows earlier lectures: a crossed-out word "CALCIUM" in grey. Bright morning light, playful mood. Label: "HER HERO" in bold above the phone and bowler.

key: In a joint family the grandmother wants
name: ch03_ragi_dosa_granddaughter
alt: A teenage granddaughter proudly serves ragi dosas to the family while filming them, and the grandmother who suggested it smiles quietly in the background.
scene: A wide view of a busy joint-family kitchen and dining area on a Sunday morning, a long steel dining table with banana leaves, a gas stove with a cast-iron tawa, jars of millets on a shelf labelled with small grain drawings. On the LEFT at the stove, the teenage granddaughter (sixteen, ponytail, oversized T-shirt and track pants, an apron) flips a dark brown ragi dosa with a confident flourish, a phone on a small tripod beside her filming her. In the CENTRE at the table, three cousins and an uncle (a boy in a cricket jersey, a girl with headphones around her neck, a younger boy, a moustached uncle in a kurta) eat dosas with chutney, nodding, one giving a thumbs-up. The granddaughter's speech bubble shows a small heart, a flexed arm and a grain of millet, meaning she is explaining the health benefits. On the RIGHT in the doorway, the grandmother (seventies, white cotton sari with a green border, spectacles, grey bun) leans on the frame holding a cup of tea, smiling a small knowing smile, with a little lightbulb drifting from her towards the granddaughter. A dashed arrow traces the lightbulb's path. Warm Sunday light, cosy mood. Label: "HER IDEA" in bold above the granddaughter.

key: A good cricket captain with a struggling
name: ch03_captain_three_steps
alt: Between overs a cricket captain talks quietly with his struggling bowler, praises his first spell and points out the batter he can dismiss.
scene: A medium-wide view of a local cricket ground on a sunny afternoon, a white sightscreen and a small stand of spectators in the background, the pitch in the middle. In the CENTRE near the boundary rope, away from the crowd, the captain (late twenties, white cricket kit, cap, sunglasses pushed up) has one arm around the shoulders of the young bowler (early twenties, white kit, sweat towel tucked in his trousers, head slightly down, ball in hand), speaking quietly to him, not shouting. Three numbered round badges float in a row above them: badge "1" shows a crossed-out shouting mouth, badge "2" shows a gold star over a small scoreboard, badge "3" shows a batter in a helmet with a short ball bouncing at his chest and a trophy. On the RIGHT in the distance, the opposing batter with "4" on his back waits at the crease leaning on his bat. A dashed arrow runs from the captain's pointing finger across the ground to the batter, and from the batter to a small trophy icon. The bowler's face is lifting, a small spark of determination. The crowd in the stands on the left looks away, not hearing them. Warm golden light, encouraging mood. Labels: "BEST SPELL" beside badge 2 and "GET NO. 4" beside badge 3.
